text:
ConocoPhillips gained 1.6% today, bouncing back after a rocky two weeks that saw the stock down 7.6% overall. The stock has recovered the last four trading days straight, climbing $6 from its low on November 9th, as crude oil prices steadied around $90 a barrel (US) and $92 (global). The company was also among the day's highlighted stock calls on CNBC's investment committee, which can draw buying interest.

The broader context here is mixed. While heating oil prices are up sharply and typically support energy companies' refining margins, that same strength is being undercut by a global supply surplus—the IEA reported that Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels a day, pushing total global supply above demand. That surplus typically puts downward pressure on oil prices and refinery profits over time, which may explain why the stock is still down significantly over the past two weeks despite today's gain.
